sections.title: Sound of the letter u
paragraphs: The letter name is (u) /u/. Its main sound is a vowel heard in the word (uno) /ˈu.no/, which means one. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. This letter has three sounds.

sections.title: How to say the sounds
paragraphs: For the first sound, lift the back of your tongue high. Push your lips forward and make a small circle. For the second sound, make this shape very quickly as you glide into another vowel. For the third sound, keep your mouth quiet and make no noise at all. Put your fingers on your throat to feel the voice buzz on the first two sounds.

sections.title: Spelling rules for this letter
paragraphs: As a regular vowel, it sounds like /u/ in (luna) /ˈlu.na/. Next to another vowel, it acts as a semivowel /w/ in (fuego) /ˈfwe.ɣo/. A semivowel is a short sound that works like a vowel but acts like a consonant. In the combinations with q or g before the vowels e or i, the letter is not pronounced, as in (queso) /ˈke.so/ and (guitarra) /ɡiˈta.ra/.

sections.title: Common mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: Do not let this vowel slide into two parts like the word boot. Keep your lips pushed forward into a tight circle from the start to the end. Do not relax it into a weak sound like the vowel in put. Never say the letter when it stands between q or g and the front vowels.
